bull_bear.body: INR110cr ECB used for Barjora line; INR180cr in FDs held; dividend recommended at INR2/share; no buybacks planned; warrants conversion to complete by July 2025 (INR1.17cr equity infusion)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global trade tariffs (US/China); oversupply from China; delay in UAE plant commissioning; polymer price volatility; customer concentration in capacitor segment
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, long-term oriented; explicitly avoids opportunistic pricing; emphasizes quality, customer relationships, and global supply chain positioning; transparent on delays and pricing rationale
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: UAE plant is strategically positioned to bypass potential US tariffs on Indian goods; solar power from Tata Power associate already paid back investment in 6 months; dielectric-grade polymers are non-commodity and not directly tied to crude oil prices
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Pioneering, dominant domestic player in dielectric films even though India has sizable zero-duty imports
- Accrued manufacturing depth, development capability, and quality discipline seen by the Board as meaningful competitive barriers
- Long-term, stable B2B relationships with an impressive list of leading Indian and transnational customers
- Barjora's dielectric film line operated at full utilization with volume maintained and a robust, domestically market-leading competitive position
- Low-leverage financial philosophy: lean balance sheet with no long-term debt beyond supplier credits against machinery
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign-exchange translation exposure on Euro-linked long-term liabilities — Reported PAT of INR 30.52 Crores was after an unrealized translation loss of INR 11.14 Crores on Euro-linked long-term liabilities, driven by the INR's broad-based weakness against major currencies; this is a recurring, non-operational item embedded in reported profit.
- Geopolitical risk at the UAE project site (Ras Al Khaimah) — The West Asian conflict escalated significantly since late February 2026, with hostilities directly affecting Gulf states including the UAE; the subsidiary's project at Ras Al Khaimah calls for particular vigilance, and conditions remain fluid, though no adverse impact to people, assets, or work at site has occurred to date.
- Global logistics and input-cost volatility from a closed shipping corridor — A critical corridor for energy, petrochemicals, and freight has been effectively closed to normal commercial shipping, and global resin, energy, and freight costs have been volatile as a result - described as active, real-time pressures on cost and logistics, not latent risks.
- Demand and pricing softness across product categories — Pricing and margins across product categories were under pressure from prevailing economic and trade headwinds, moderating profits and reflected in PBIDT performance versus the prior year.
- End-market concentration/cyclicality in coextruded sheets & refrigerator liners — Volumes in this segment are directly correlated to consumer end-market conditions in the refrigerator sector; a decline in refrigerator volumes already led to a modest decrease in off-take, a sectoral dynamic the Company does not consider structural but which remains an exposure.
- Zero-duty import competition in dielectric films — Xpro is the pioneering, dominant domestic player in dielectric films, even as India has sizable imports of dielectric films at zero-duty, an ongoing competitive pressure on the Company's core segment.
- Execution and ramp-up risk on new capacity — The new Barjora dielectric film line (commissioned March 27, 2026) faces a calibrated ramp-up with performance building as volumes scale; earlier delays in the project were externally driven, and the pace of the broader 4,000-to-13,000 MT India+UAE capacity scale-up will hinge on global stability and market clarity.
- Regulatory change raising labour-related costs — The consolidation of multiple labour laws into four Labour Codes, effective November 2025, revised the definition of wages, requiring recognition of an incremental past service cost of INR 1.39 Crores (covering gratuity and compensated absences); further notifications are expected and will need to be accounted for as they arise.

business.body: Xpro India is a polymer processor manufacturing semi-finished plastic products: Dielectric/Capacitor Films (Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene films), Coextruded Cast Films, and Coextruded Sheets & Thermoformed Refrigerator Liners. It sells mainly B2B to leading Indian and transnational companies with long-standing, stable relationships, including capacitor/metalliser manufacturers, white-goods makers, and tyre and hygiene-products manufacturers.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Dielectric/Capacitor Films:** Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP) dielectric films, including plain smooth films modified for good metallization and winding hazy/rough films
- **Coextruded Sheets/Thermoformed Refrigerator Liners:** Refrigerator inner and door liners, automotive interior and exterior trims, furniture, luggage shells, sanitary products (bathtubs, cabinets, electrical/electronic housings)
- **Coextruded Cast Films:** Release film for the tyre and tread segment, special hygiene films (diaper backing film, under-pads, adult incontinent products, sanitary napkins, surgical drapes)

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not disclosed; customer commitments confirmed for Barjora line; UAE line targeting global buyers
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: UAE plant enables export to US/EU; PLI-driven capacitor manufacturing boom in India; metallized film import substitution; potential for downstream capacitor manufacturing JV
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build a globally significant, India-led dielectric films business, leveraging core expertise in extrusion, coextrusion, and biaxially oriented dielectric films
- Scale aggregate India+UAE dielectric film capacity from 4,000 MT to 13,000 MT between 2025 and 2027, funded predominantly with equity consistent with a low-leverage philosophy
- Roadmap includes a fourth dielectric film line in the UAE (land already secured) and a fifth line in India
- Pursue ultra-thin films and related niche segments as the next stratum of technical ambition, leveraging precision manufacturing heritage for a credible head start
- Assess options for downstream value-addition opportunities in dielectrics, and select non-dielectric segments where process and materials expertise can confer an advantage
- Planned senior management realignment: Girish Behal appointed President & CEO (27/8/2025) and proposed as Managing Director effective January 1, 2027, as C Bhaskar's 26-year executive board tenure ends December 31, 2026
- Dividend of INR 2.00 per ordinary share (face value INR 10) proposed for the year ended March 31, 2026, to be put to shareholders at the AGM on July 20, 2026. Committee/Board sitting fees for Directors (other than the Chairman and Managing Director) were revised w.e.f. April 1, 2026. Remuneration for the Chairman and Managing Director may be fixed periodically by the Board within Companies Act limits, with the Chairman's remuneration capped at Rs. 25 lacs per month.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Commissioned the new dielectric film line at Barjora on March 27, 2026, doubling the Company's nameplate dielectric film capacity in India from 4,000 to 8,000 MT annually - described as the Company's most significant and highest-value expansion to date, with the Board anticipating a calibrated ramp-up as volumes scale. In parallel, the UAE subsidiary Xpro Dielectric Films FZ-LLC's dielectric films project at Ras Al Khaimah received the full planned equity funding from the parent and is advancing, currently in implementation/pre-revenue stage. Between 2025 and 2027, Xpro's aggregate annual dielectric film capacity across India and UAE is planned to scale from 4,000 MT to 13,000 MT, funded predominantly with equity consistent with the Company's low-leverage philosophy; a fourth dielectric film line is referenced as part of this roadmap (detail truncated in the source text provided).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Softness in end-markets, with pricing and margins under pressure from prevailing economic and trade headwinds, moderated profits despite maintained competitiveness and financial prudence
- Barjora's dielectric film line operated at full utilization with volume maintained; competitive position remains robust with domestic market leadership
- Coextruded sheets/refrigerator liners volumes are directly correlated to consumer end-market conditions; a decline in refrigerator volumes led to a modest off-take decrease, viewed as sectoral, not structural
- New Barjora dielectric line: earlier delays were externally driven and are behind the Company; a calibrated ramp-up is anticipated with performance building as volumes scale
- India's broader economic conditions viewed as resilient, though the RBI has flagged downside risks from geopolitical events, crude oil prices, and potential climate-related disruptions
- Company positions its India-centric, high-technology dielectric films business (import-reducing, export-generating) as aligned with national priorities of economic caution, self-reliance, and forex conservation
- West Asian conflict (escalated since late February 2026) and closure of a critical shipping corridor for energy/petrochemicals/freight are creating active, real-time pressures on cost and logistics, with volatile global resin, energy, and freight costs

deepdive.thesis: Xpro India delivered 15% revenue growth in FY25 driven by Coex division expansion, but EBITDA margin compressed due to strategic pricing cuts in dielectric films to preempt capacity glut from two new lines. The critical inflection point is imminent commissioning of the Barjora line in June 2025 and UAE plant by Q4CY25, which will double capacity and unlock higher-margin export revenue.
